approach: Add a `[disk] min_free_gb` setting (an Option, default 10 when absent, left out of the config digest) and a small `disk` module in athena-core. The free-space reader is a plain `fn` held in `StateDir`, beside the existing `remover`, so tests swap it with `with_free_space` and no `Athena { .. }` literal changes. `dispatch` calls a `disk_gate` before any commit. If free space is below the minimum, it sweeps idle workspaces' `target/` (any `jobs/<id>/` whose job lock can be taken, which skips locked ones and the job being dispatched). It re-reads free space. If still low, it writes a small hold marker `<state>/holds/<job>.json` (free and required bytes) and returns a new `GoResult::Held`, so the job stays Proposed. The same gate runs in the verification step before `verifier_snapshot`. If still low there, the job closes `Failed` through the existing `failure()`, with a reason starting `environment: low disk`, and no marker is written. `athena retry` then applies unchanged. In drain, `Run` gains `held`, which maps through `RunStep::Held` and `ItemEnd::Held` exactly as `needs_accepting` does: not a failure, the item stays queued, and a later drain runs the same job id. Status and drain output show 'environment: low disk' with the free and required amounts. A successful dispatch clears the marker.

decisions.choice: The check runs at two places in the core: the top of `dispatch` (before the prediction commit, pin and any agent) and in the verification step before `verifier_snapshot`. A dispatch hold returns a new `GoResult::Held`. A pre-checks shortfall closes the job `Failed` through the existing `failure()`.
decisions.reason: This is the user's decision: a hold only at dispatch, and a retryable environment failure before the checks. `Failed` is already what `athena retry` accepts and what drain retries. Nothing is left Dispatched with a marker.

rejected.option: A mid-run hold and a resume route
rejected.why: Out of scope by the user's decision.

rejected.option: Rejecting the job on low disk
rejected.why: Rejection means the work was refused. Low disk is the environment, so it must stay retryable and not count as a rejection.

decisions.choice: Keep the free-space reader as a `fn(&Path) -> io::Result<u64>` field on `StateDir` (`with_free_space`). The real one runs `df -Pk <path>`.
decisions.reason: It follows the existing `with_remover` pattern, changes no `Athena` struct literals, and keeps the type `Clone` and `Debug`. athena-core has no libc or statvfs dependency, and adding one would touch Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, which are not deliverables.

rejected.option: A new `Athena` field or trait object
rejected.why: Every `Athena { .. }` construction would have to change.
It edits manifests that are not deliverables.

decisions.choice: Make `Config.disk` an `Option<DiskConfig>` with `skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none"`, reset to None in `reading_inputs`, with an accessor `min_free_gb()` that returns the default 10.
decisions.reason: This copies how `job_plan` is handled. The serialized config, and so every stored config digest, stays byte-identical, so no reading is invalidated and athena.toml stays untouched.

rejected.why: It adds a key to the serialized config, which moves every digest and forces rereads.

decisions.choice: Persist a hold as a marker file `<state>/holds/<job>.json`, written on a dispatch hold and removed when the job dispatches, closes or is held no more. Status reads it and shows `environment: low disk (free X, required Y)` through a new optional `hold` on `JobLine`. The job's state name stays `proposed`.
decisions.reason: A hold is local to this machine and needs no record or commit. Keeping the state name stops the open-work filter and the 'next' hints from changing.

rejected.why: It writes to the history on every held drain and adds a record type.

rejected.option: Computing the hold live in status
rejected.why: Status would then probe the disk. It could not show the amounts that blocked the dispatch.

decisions.choice: The idle sweep removes only `jobs/<id>/target` and tries `try_lock_job` first. A locked job is skipped, and so is the job being dispatched, whose own lock is held. Closed jobs are covered because their directories are already removed at close (173d12e). A leftover closed directory is unlocked and is swept too.
decisions.reason: This reuses the existing remover and job-lock helpers, and leaves source, snapshots and live records alone.

rejected.why: It would destroy kept snapshots and live records of interrupted jobs.

decisions.choice: Drain mirrors `needs_accepting`: `Run.held`, `RunStep::Held`, `ItemEnd::Held`. Outcome text is 'environment: low disk' and the reason carries the free and required amounts. Drain adds a note line, and `finish` treats Held like Idle/NeedsAccepting.
decisions.reason: It is the proven pattern for 'left queued, not a failure', and a later drain re-reads the queue and picks up the same job id.

rejected.option: Counting a hold as a failed attempt
rejected.why: It would trigger a retry and the RepeatedFailure stop.

files.purpose: Add `DiskConfig { min_free_gb }`, `Config.disk: Option<DiskConfig>` (skip_serializing_if none), `DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_GB = 10`, `min_free_gb()`, reset in `reading_inputs`, and tests.
The `df -Pk` free-space reader, `Low { free, required }` text, the idle `target/` sweep, hold marker read, write and clear, and `Athena::disk_gate`, with unit tests.
Add the `free_space` fn field, `with_free_space`, `free_bytes`, `remove_target(job)`, `jobs_dir` listing and `hold_file(job)`.

Add `GoResult::Held(Box<Held>)`. Call `disk_gate` at the top of `dispatch` after the config check and clear the marker once dispatched. Call it before `verifier_snapshot` and fail with the environment reason.
Add `JobLine.hold: Option<String>` from the marker, with 'environment: low disk' and the amounts.
Render the hold text on the status job lines and in the `athena go` output for a Held result.
Add `Run.held`, `RunStep::Held`, `ItemEnd::Held`, the outcome and reason text and a note; map `GoResult::Held` in `RealSteps::run` and `read`.
Handle the new `GoResult::Held` arm in `go_and_report` (message and exit code 2, JSON included). Not on the brief's list, but the match must be exhaustive.
Add the real-steps hold-then-run test, the status and drain text test and the failure-not-counted test.
Record the setting, the dispatch hold and the pre-checks failure under Unreleased, saying 'the user'.
Document `[disk] min_free_gb` (default 10), the 'environment: low disk' status and what the user does.

steps: config.rs: add DiskConfig, the Option field with skip_serializing_if, DEFAULT_MIN_FREE_GB, the accessor, the reset in reading_inputs, and tests (default 10, parse, digest unchanged).

state.rs: add the `free_space` fn field (default the real reader), `with_free_space`, `free_bytes(path)`, `remove_target(job)` through the remover, a listing of job ids under `jobs/`, and `hold_file(job)`.

disk.rs: write the `df -Pk` reader. Write `Low` with Display ('free X, required Y' via `format_bytes`). Write `sweep_idle_targets` (try_lock_job, skip on None, remove `target/`, return the bytes reclaimed). Write hold marker write, read and clear. Write `Athena::disk_gate(jc, job, ui) -> Option<Low>`: probe, then sweep and re-probe if low. Unit-test the sweep with a held lock.

run.rs: add `GoResult::Held`. In `dispatch`, call the gate after the config digest check and before pin_repo or any commit; on Low write the marker, print an 'environment: low disk' line and return Held; on success clear the marker. In the verification step, call the gate before `verifier_snapshot`; on Low set `closing.happened = self.failure(ctx, "environment: low disk before the checks: free X, required Y; free space, then `athena retry <job>`")` and return Ok(closing). Update match sites in core tests (`test_support.rs` `landed`).
status.rs and display.rs: add `JobLine.hold` filled for proposed jobs that have a marker; render it. main.rs: add the Held arm.
drain.rs: add the held plumbing mirroring needs_accepting, including the doc comment at the top of the module and the Held arm in `RealSteps::read`/`run`.
Write core tests (criteria 1, 2, 4, 5) with a static-atomic fake free-space fn, and the drain tests (criterion 3) with the real steps in tests/drain.rs.
Update CHANGELOG.md and README.md. Check that neither says 'operator'.
Run cargo fmt --all, then cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings, then cargo test --locked.

risks.risk: `df` is missing or its output differs, so the real reader fails.
risks.mitigation: On a read error, treat free space as unknown and carry on, printing one warning line. Never hold or fail on an error. Parse `df -Pk` (POSIX format), which is stable. Tests use the injected fn.

risks.risk: Adding a `GoResult` variant breaks matches in other crates' tests (lifecycle, retry, steward, job_plan, history_pr_head, run_pin_tests).
risks.mitigation: The existing arms are `Finished`/`Reread` with a wildcard or panic arm; compile and add an arm only where the match is exhaustive. Most are `let ... else` patterns and keep working.

risks.risk: The sweep deletes the `target/` of a job that is about to run in another process.
risks.mitigation: It takes the job lock with `try_lock_job` and skips on contention. The job being dispatched holds its own lock (flock is per open file), so it is skipped too.

risks.risk: A stale hold marker lingers after the job is closed or dispatched.
risks.mitigation: Clear it on dispatch and when the job closes. Status shows a hold only for a job still in the Proposed state.

risks.risk: Parallel drain workers all sweep at once.
risks.mitigation: A sweep that cannot take a lock skips it, and removing a missing `target/` is a no-op.

risks.risk: The config digest changes and forces rereads.
risks.mitigation: `disk` is an Option left out when None and reset in `reading_inputs`; a test compares the digest with and without the section.

demonstrations.method: A core/CLI test plants an idle job directory with `target/` and a source file. It sets `with_free_space` to a fake reporting 3 GB until the planted `target/` is gone, then 50 GB. It runs `go` on a queued, read job with a UI that records lines, and asserts the sweep line and removal come before the 'dispatched' line. A second test does the same before the checks: the sweep line comes before the first check line, and the planted `target/` is gone by then.
demonstrations.observes: The sweep line and the removal of `target/` come before 'dispatched' and before the first check line, with the fake reporting low only until the sweep.
demonstrations.fails_without: If `dispatch` or the pre-checks gate did not sweep first, `target/` would still exist and no sweep line would appear before dispatch or the checks.

demonstrations.method: A test uses a fake that stays at 3 GB, plants an idle `target/` and runs `go` and then status. It asserts `GoResult::Held` is returned and no 'dispatched' line or prediction commit exists. The job state is still proposed and not closed or rejected. The StatusView `JobLine.hold` and the status text contain 'environment: low disk', the free amount and the 10.0 GB required. The drain report line has the same outcome and amounts.
demonstrations.observes: Held, not rejected, no dispatch commit, and the text with both amounts in status and drain output.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the hold, the job would be dispatched or rejected, and status would show plain 'proposed' with no amounts.

demonstrations.method: A drain test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs uses the real steps (`RealSteps::live`, like the existing real-steps test around line 1050) with a fake free-space function backed by a static atomic. First drain at low disk: the report has outcome 'environment: low disk', failed count 0, stop is not RepeatedFailure, and the job is still queued. Then set the atomic high and drain again: the same job id runs to a verdict (landed or passed).
demonstrations.observes: No failure counted on the first drain, and the second drain's JobLine carries the same job id with a verdict.
demonstrations.fails_without: If the hold were mapped as a failure or created a new job, the first drain would report a failure or the second would run a different id.

demonstrations.method: A core test fakes free space low at the pre-checks gate (high at dispatch) and stays low after the sweep. It asserts the closed state is Failed (not Rejected), the reason starts with 'environment: low disk' and names retry, `holds/<job>.json` does not exist, and no check ran. A second case frees the space after the first probe and asserts verification proceeds and the checks run.
demonstrations.observes: Failed with a retryable environment reason, no marker, and verification going ahead once space is free.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the gate, the checks would run on a full disk and the job would fail later with an opaque build error, or the state would be Rejected.

demonstrations.method: A unit test in disk.rs builds a StateDir in a tempdir with three job directories: one unlocked with `target/` and a source file, one with `target/` whose `job.lock` is held through `try_lock_job`, and one with no `target/`. It runs the sweep. It asserts the first `target/` is gone and its source file remains, and the locked job's `target/` is intact.
demonstrations.observes: `target/` removed, source kept, locked workspace untouched.
demonstrations.fails_without: A sweep that ignored the lock would remove the locked job's `target/`, and one that removed the whole directory would lose the source file.

demonstrations.method: A config.rs unit test parses `athena.toml` and a toml with `[disk] min_free_gb = 3` and checks `min_free_gb()` is 10 and 3. A second test checks `reading_inputs` is equal with and without a `[disk]` section. `git diff` shows athena.toml unchanged. README and CHANGELOG are read to confirm they name `[disk] min_free_gb` and 'environment: low disk' and say 'the user'.
demonstrations.observes: The default is 10, the digest is unmoved, and `git diff` names no athena.toml. The docs name the setting and status and contain no 'operator'.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the default in config.rs, the absent-setting test would not find 10, and a plain serialized field would change the digest.

open_questions: main.rs is not in the brief's deliverables, but the exhaustive match in `go_and_report` needs a Held arm, so the plan touches it. The producer should report this.
The real free-space reader shells out to `df -Pk` because athena-core has no libc or statvfs dependency. Say if a dependency is acceptable instead.

Whether `athena retry` accepts a job closed Failed with this reason was read from the drain mapping (Failed maps to retry) but its own checks in the retry route were not read; the producer should confirm with a test that retries it.
